Reusing Scope for a Single Ticket

The exact same scopeForViewer fragment guards both the list and one ticket by id — so they can never quietly disagree.

scopeForViewer (previous slide) is called from two places, not one — the list endpoint, merged alongside the existing status filter, and getTicketById, which swaps from findUnique to findFirst to make room for it:

// Figure 4.12: the same scope, combined with a status filter or an id (src/services/ticket.service.js, excerpt)
export const getAllTickets = async ({ status, sortBy, order, page, pageSize }, viewer) => {
  const where = { ...scopeForViewer(viewer), ...(status ? { status } : {}) };
  // ...findMany/count using `where`, unchanged from Lesson 3...
};

export const getTicketById = async (id, viewer) =>
  prisma.ticket.findFirst({
    where: { id, ...scopeForViewer(viewer) },
    include: { customer: userSummary, assignedAgent: userSummary },
  });

{ ...scopeForViewer(viewer), ...(status ? { status } : {}) } spreads both fragments into one object — Prisma treats multiple top-level keys in a where (including one named OR, an agent's shape from the previous slide) as an implicit and, so this reads as "in scope for this viewer, and matching the status filter if one was given" — never one replacing the other.

findFirst, not findUnique, is the change worth noticing on getTicketById: findUnique's where only ever accepts a unique field (here, id) — it has no way to also apply an OR alongside it. findFirst takes any where shape at all, at the cost of no longer guaranteeing the result is the unique row (Prisma just returns the first match) — a non-issue here, since id alone can only ever match zero or one ticket regardless of what else is in the where object.

The payoff of reusing one scopeForViewer in both places: there's no way for the list endpoint and the single-ticket endpoint to define "visible to this viewer" even slightly differently, the way there would be if each wrote its own scoping logic by hand.
